title: Restaurant Rating Causal Attribution
subtitle: DAG construction, DoWhy identification, mediation, and heterogeneous effects
summary: A four-phase causal analysis that asks not just what correlates with restaurant ratings but what causes them and through which pathways. It builds a 31-node causal graph, estimates effects with DoWhy backdoor adjustment against a Shapley-value correlational baseline, then decomposes those effects with Baron & Kenny mediation and IPW-based heterogeneous treatment effects across 17 pathways.
problem: Attribution analysis usually stops at feature importance, which answers 'what moves with the outcome' and is routinely misread as 'what moves the outcome'. The gap matters: acting on an inflated correlational estimate wastes budget. This project makes the gap measurable by running both methods on the same data and comparing them directly.
goals: Construct an explicit causal graph and identify treatment variables.
Estimate causal effects via backdoor adjustment and quantify how far they sit from naive correlations.
Decompose effects into direct and mediated components.
Test whether effects differ across customer subgroups.
non_goals: Prediction — no model is trained to forecast ratings.
Establishing generalizable findings about restaurants outside the study pool.
requirements: Single canonical data source for all downstream phases
Met — every module imports get_initial_data() from 01_Data_Analysis/data_pipeline.py
Formal causal identification, not ad-hoc regression
Met — DoWhy backdoor identification against the declared graph
Report the correlational baseline alongside the causal estimate

Decompose effects through mediators and across subgroups

data.sources: UCI Restaurant & Consumer Data — 9 relational CSVs merged to 31,559 rows × 52 features
data.pipeline: Nine CSVs joined via pandas left merges (user chain and restaurant chain, combined on placeID), then engineered: Haversine distance, KMeans location clusters (k=5), age groups, Jaccard cuisine-match score, business-hours categories. '?' replaced with NaN, most-frequent imputation across 17 categorical columns, then label encoding.
data.notes: Profiling shows zero remaining nulls across all 52 columns — because imputation already ran, so observed and imputed values are indistinguishable downstream. The left-join fan-out also means 31,559 rows represent far fewer unique user-restaurant pairs, so unweighted regressions implicitly weight users by how many payment methods and cuisines they list.

candidates: Selected as the primary causal estimator
selected: DoWhy backdoor adjustment as the headline estimator, reported against Shapley attribution, with mediation and IPW-HTE for decomposition.
selection_rationale: The comparison is the finding. DoWhy's graph-informed estimate for food_rating is 0.549 against a naive correlation of 0.864 — the 0.315 gap is confounding made visible, and it is the number a stakeholder should care about when sizing an investment. Mediation then shows that activity's effect is essentially entirely indirect (100.2%), which changes the intervention from 'increase activity' to 'improve food and service, which activity was proxying for'.

evaluation.strategy: No train/test split — this is estimation, not prediction. Validity rests on the declared graph and the backdoor criterion. The correlational baseline serves as the reference point for how much confounding the adjustment removes.
evaluation.baseline: Naive Shapley-value attribution on the same data.
metrics: 31 nodes, 78 edges, 7 direct treatments, 53 cycles detected

architecture: data_pipeline.py: merge, engineer, impute, encode → final_data.pkl
Reports/ and results/ directories per phase
dataflow: final_data.pkl → causal graph construction → causal_graph.png, path summary
graph + data → DoWhy backdoor identification → causal effect estimates
graph + data → Shapley / OLS → correlational baseline
data → mediation and IPW-HTE → mediation_summary.csv, HTE reports

deployment.current: Not deployed. Phase modules are run individually; final_data.pkl is cached so downstream phases do not re-run the merge. pyproject.toml and requirements.txt define the environment.
deployment.gaps: No orchestration across the four phases, no assertion that the cached pickle matches the current pipeline code, and pickle as a cache format is both version-fragile and unsafe to load from an untrusted source.

monitoring.current: Each phase writes a text report to its Reports/ or results/ directory, so a run leaves an audit trail.
monitoring.gaps: No sensitivity analysis to unmeasured confounding, no refutation tests, and no check that the graph's assumptions still hold if the data is refreshed.

risks: The causal graph contains 53 cycles and is not a strict DAG, which undermines every identification claim
Disclosed in the README, model card, and this document. Resolving it is the top roadmap item.
Demographic 'treatments' — height, personality, color preference — have no plausible causal mechanism on ratings
Significant estimates for these are presented as evidence of residual confounding, not as real effects.
Imputation is baked into the cached artifact, so imputed and observed values are indistinguishable downstream
Documented in the data card; adding imputation indicators is a roadmap item.
Join fan-out silently weights users by their number of payment methods and cuisines
Documented; inverse-frequency weighting is a roadmap item.
roadmap: Enumerate the cycles, trace each to the feature-engineering interaction that created it, and either remove the derived node or orient the edge on domain grounds until the graph is acyclic. Re-run DoWhy afterward and report how the estimates move
Run DoWhy's built-in refuters — placebo treatment, random common cause, data subset — and publish the results next to each estimate
Emit a parallel `_was_imputed` indicator column per imputed field and include the indicators as covariates
Either deduplicate to unique user–restaurant pairs or apply inverse-frequency weights, and compare estimates before and after
No sensitivity analysis to unmeasured confounding
Add E-value or Rosenbaum bounds so each headline effect carries a statement of how strong a hidden confounder would need to be to overturn it
Pickle cache is version-fragile and unsafe
Switch to parquet with an explicit schema, and assert a pipeline-code hash matches the cache before use
Wrap in a single runner with a config file, matching the run_all.py pattern used elsewhere in the portfolio
Findings limited to a 2012 Mexican convenience sample
Replicate on a second ratings dataset to test whether the mediation structure holds
open_questions: After the cycles are resolved, does food_rating's effect stay near 0.549 or move materially? The current estimate is conditional on a graph that does not satisfy DoWhy's assumptions.
Is 'activity is 100.2% mediated' a real full-mediation result or an artifact of measurement overlap between activity and the mediators?
Should the demographic treatments be dropped from the analysis entirely rather than reported with caveats?
